questions.question: int a[] = {10,20,30,40}; int *p = a; p = p + 2; printf("%d", *p);  What is printed?
questions.solutionApproach: p starts at a[0]. p+2 moves 2 ints ahead → points to a[2]=30.

questions.question: int* makeIt() { int x = 42; return &x; }  Is it safe to dereference the pointer returned by makeIt()?
questions.solutionApproach: x is a local (stack) variable — its storage is deallocated once makeIt() returns. The returned pointer is dangling. Undefined behavior to dereference it.
questions.answer: No — dangling pointer, x's stack storage no longer exists after return.

questions.question: What does 'char *(*f[10])(int)' declare?
questions.solutionApproach: Right-left rule: f is an array[10] of (pointer to (function(int) returning (pointer to char))). So: f is an array of 10 pointers to functions, each taking an int and returning a char*.
questions.answer: f is an array of 10 pointers to functions that take an int argument and return a char*.

questions.question: void inc(int *p) { (*p)++; } int main() { int x=5; inc(&x); inc(&x); printf("%d",x); }  What is printed?
questions.solutionApproach: Each inc(&x) call increments x directly via the pointer. Starting at 5, two increments → 7.
